current_versions.typescript: 7.0.2 current stable (native Go port, GA 2026-07-08); 6.0.3 is the last JavaScript-codebase release and the supported sidecar for API consumers (7.0 announcement re-fetched this pass)
current_versions.@typescript/native-preview: Superseded/frozen at 7.0 dev builds; nightlies now ship as typescript@next - the 'tsgo' name is preview-era (announcement, re-fetched)
current_versions.biome: Current single-binary formatter+linter on the Biome 2.x line (2.5 line current in 2026) with official migrate commands from ESLint and Prettier; the guide now pins it in biome.json as its only format+lint stack
current_versions.eslint/typescript-eslint: Still the type-aware lint stack, but under TS 7 it must consume the TypeScript 6 API via the @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package (no programmatic API in TS 7.0; new API expected in 7.1)
current_versions.prettier: Still maintained as a formatter-only tool; no longer part of the guide's prescribed stack after the Biome-only adoption (judgment call (a))
current_versions.typescript-language-server (ts_ls): Community LSP wrapper around the TS 6 API; TS 7 ships its own native language server - ts_ls remains usable only against the 6.x API surface

assertions_contracts.guide_position: User-defined assertion signatures must actually test and narrow unknown; never use ! or casts to bypass external validation; console.assert does not terminate; internal invariant failures may throw, expected failures use the declared result contract.
assertions_contracts.best_practice: Consistent with the handbook's narrowing documentation the guide cites; TS 6/7 did not change assertion-signature semantics.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Guide Sec.4 re-read fresh; no assertion-model change in the 6.0 release notes or the 7.0 announcement (re-fetched this pass).

bounded_work.guide_position: Named *_MAX bounds for item count, item size, nesting, cumulative bytes, concurrent and waiting work, elapsed time and retry amplification; retries need idempotency, a shared deadline, bounded backoff and injected jitter.
bounded_work.best_practice: No official TypeScript/Node source prescribes budgets; nothing contradicts bounded admission. TS 7's parallel checker is a compiler-internal change and does not relax application-level bounding.
bounded_work.evidence: Stricter-than-mainstream Tiger policy; no contradicting official position found in the 6.0 notes or the 7.0 announcement (re-fetched).

concurrency.guide_position: Pass AbortSignal where supported; Promise.race timeout is not cancellation; bounded task registry; abort owned work on teardown and await settlement; reject stale results before commit; workers for CPU isolation with separate shared-memory policy.
concurrency.best_practice: AbortSignal-based cancellation remains the platform idiom in current Node/Web docs; TS 7 changes compiler parallelism (--checkers/--builders), not the application async model.
concurrency.evidence: Guide Sec.21 re-read fresh; the 7.0 announcement's parallelization flags (re-fetched) concern tsc itself; application concurrency rules are untouched by 6.0/7.0.

error_handling.guide_position: Discriminated Result<T,E> for expected failures (or the subsystem's declared contract), typed thrown errors handled at one boundary, catch values as unknown, every started promise awaited or owned, causes preserved, secrets redacted from serialized errors.
error_handling.best_practice: No official source prescribes Result vs exceptions; both remain in mainstream use and TS 6/7 made no change here. Handling thrown values as unknown matches strict-mode useUnknownInCatchVariables behaviour.
error_handling.evidence: Guide Sec.7 re-read fresh; neither the 6.0 release notes nor the 7.0 announcement (re-fetched) alter catch-variable or error semantics.

formatting.guide_position: One pinned formatter and lint profile everywhere it matters: SKILL operating rules, full guide Sec.23, and the Sec.27 validation recipe (biome ci .) now all prescribe Biome alone, pinned in biome.json, for format and lint (remediation judgment call (a), the Biome-only pilot adopted).
formatting.best_practice: Judged on its merits against Biome's current official state, the prescription is sound: Biome 2.x is a maintained single formatter+linter whose official site ships migrate commands from both ESLint and Prettier, i.e. it is designed to occupy exactly the combined slot the guide now gives it. Its known limit is unchanged: Biome provides no type-aware rules equivalent to typescript-eslint's, which the guide keeps available via the Sec.27 side-by-side install rather than via the format/lint stack.
formatting.evidence: Adoption VERIFIED in current text: SKILL.md operating rules ('One pinned formatter and lint profile: Biome, pinned in biome.json'), guide Sec.23 (same sentence), and Sec.27 recipe ('./node_modules/.bin/biome ci .') all agree; no prettier/eslint command survives in the recipe. Run-1's internal-muddle basis for stale is gone.

memory_ownership.guide_position: Bound maps/caches/strings/buffers/queued promises/worker messages; Promise.all starts all work eagerly so bound admission before creating promises; short views can retain large ArrayBuffers; one owner per resource with try/finally dispose/close; FinalizationRegistry is not cleanup; disposal syntax only where runtime/toolchain support is verified.
memory_ownership.best_practice: Ownership/bounding claims remain sound; the guide's disposal hedge is conditional rather than wrong, and no official 6.0/7.0 change affects its retention or admission claims.
memory_ownership.evidence: Guide Sec.14/Sec.15 re-read fresh (try/finally + explicit dispose/close, FinalizationRegistry caveat intact); 7.0 announcement (re-fetched) contains no contrary change.

security.guide_position: Never eval/new Function on untrusted data; no innerHTML for text; type checker is not a sandbox; argv-form spawn/execFile with shell:false; path normalization is not authorization and startsWith is not containment; temp file in destination dir then rename; committed lockfile with frozen CI installs; review install scripts/native addons.
security.best_practice: Aligns with current Node child_process guidance the guide cites; the type system remains non-sandboxing. TS 6/7 introduce no contrary guidance.
security.evidence: Guide Sec.18-20 re-read fresh; no 2026 change to those security semantics was found in the sources fetched this pass.

static_analysis.guide_position: Gate on tsc --noEmit plus the pinned Biome lint profile; Sec.27 now carries the API caveat (remediation item 16): TS 7.0 ships no programmatic compiler API (new API expected in 7.1), so API consumers such as typescript-eslint run against the documented side-by-side install - typescript@^7.0.2 for checking, typescript aliased to npm:@typescript/typescript6 for API consumers; Biome does not consume the compiler API and is unaffected.
static_analysis.best_practice: Exactly Microsoft's documented pattern: the 7.0 announcement's side-by-side section names typescript-eslint explicitly as a tool that still needs the 6.0 API and documents the @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package with the npm-alias install.
static_analysis.evidence: Remediation item 16 VERIFIED in current text: Sec.27 contains the caveat, the 7.1 expectation, both pins, and the Biome-unaffected note, in substance verbatim. Announcement section re-fetched this pass and matches.

testing.guide_position: Decoder tests over null/undefined/booleans/fractional/NaN/infinity/unsafe integers/sparse arrays/oversize/prototype-like keys; rejection also tested under emitted JavaScript; half validation / half adversarial split.
testing.best_practice: Nothing in TS 6/7 changes this; testing emitted JS remains necessary because type stripping/erasure behaviour is unchanged in the native port (7.0 is a faithful port of 6.0 semantics).
testing.evidence: Guide Sec.28 re-read fresh; the 7.0 announcement (re-fetched) describes the port as deliberately faithful to 6.0 structure and results.

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Header and Sec.2 now declare a TypeScript 7.0 strict profile (6.0 API sidecar where tooling requires it) with ES2025+; SKILL description declares TypeScript 7.0+ with a current ES target and explicit target/rootDir/types; Sec.27 pins typescript@^7.0.2. Residual inconsistencies remain in SKILL Workflow step 1 ('TypeScript version (5.9+)') and the Sec.23 example tsconfig (target ES2022 / module CommonJS) - see mechanical_fixes; the Sec.23 tsconfig rebuild itself remains a proposal.
toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current release is TypeScript 7.0 (7.0.2), the native Go port, GA 2026-07-08. TS 6.0 was the last JavaScript-codebase release and the bridge: strict on by default, types defaulting to [], module/target defaults changed, and baseUrl, node10/classic resolution, target es5 and several module kinds deprecated there and hard errors in 7. @typescript/native-preview is superseded; nightlies ship as typescript@next.
toolchain_pins.evidence: Pass-1 re-pin VERIFIED in current text: guide header, Sec.2, SKILL description and Sec.27 all state the 7.0 baseline (the 5.9 profile claims are gone from those surfaces). Official 7.0 announcement re-fetched in full this pass (no-API caveat, side-by-side package, native-preview superseded). Residual 5.9+/ES2022 surfaces are recorded as mechanical fixes rather than scored stale, because the guide's declared baseline - the load-bearing claim - is now current and consistent across header, assumptions and recipe.

proposals.proposal: Promote the Sec.27 caveat to a standing dual-install policy: pin typescript@^7.0.2 as the checking compiler (native tsc) and alias typescript to npm:@typescript/typescript6 for API consumers (typescript-eslint and any custom transformers), with CI running the native tsc as the authoritative gate, and a note that a type the native check rejects can still look green in an editor resolving through the 6.x alias. Carried forward from run 1: the facts were added by remediation item 16, the adoption as stated policy was not.
proposals.evidence: The 7.0 announcement's side-by-side section documents exactly this alias pattern, names typescript-eslint as the motivating consumer, and states a new API is expected in 7.1 (section re-fetched this pass).
proposals.recommendation: Adopt now; drop the sidecar only when the lint stack runs on the 7.1 API.

proposals.proposal: Rebuild the Section 23 example tsconfig for the 6/7 world: write every load-bearing option explicitly (the guide's own philosophy), set rootDir and types explicitly instead of inheriting the new defaults, use nodenext or bundler resolution, and add a short 'removed in 7.0, never use' list (baseUrl, node10/classic resolution, target es5, amd/umd/systemjs modules, outFile, esModuleInterop:false). Carried forward from run 1 unadopted; the Sec.23 block still shows target ES2022 / module CommonJS (see mechanical_fixes).
proposals.evidence: 6.0 release notes deprecate baseUrl (no longer a resolution root) and the December 2025 TS7 progress post lists the changed defaults (strict on, target floats to latest ES, rootDir = tsconfig directory) and the options 7.0 removes.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt with the version re-pin; keep the CommonJS standalone-example note but mark it as an example-local exception.
